mainTopic: טבול יום at מתן תורה, how long שכבת זרע stays טמא, and the dispute over the date and weekday of מתן תורה
overview: The גמרא asks how the תורה could be given when some women may have been טבולי יום at Sinai. Two אמוראים answer that the תורה can be given to a טבול יום, and מרימר clarifies that this only means it was fit to be given that way. רבי יצחק then explains why the immersion was not moved to twilight or to שבת morning: the תורה had to be given in daylight, and the whole nation had to arrive together. Next, רבי יוחנן reports that חכמים require six full עונות, and רב חסדא limits the dispute to semen discharged from a woman, defending this against רב ששת's challenge. רב פפא asks about semen inside a גויה and inside a בהמה, and both questions end in תיקו. Finally, a ברייתא records a מחלוקת over whether the עשרת הדברות were given on the 6th or 7th of סיון. רבא shows that both sides agree the people arrived at סיני on ראש חודש and that the תורה was given on שבת. The real dispute is which weekday ראש חודש fell on, and רבי יוסי's day-by-day timeline begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Weren't some of the people only immersed that same day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the Sinai timeline: some women would have had to immerse that day, so at מתן תורה they were only טבולי יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But weren't they people who had immersed that same day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the timeline it has been building for מתן תורה. Under that count, some women would have become טמא, immersed, and still been טבול יום when the תורה was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום has already gone to the מקוה but is not fully טהור until nightfall. The challenge assumes the תורה should be given to a nation that is completely pure. So a timeline that leaves anyone as a טבול יום looks problematic.

keyTerms.meaning: People who immersed today and are not fully pure until sunset
But isn't it so that… (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: A טבול יום is not fully טמא. He has already immersed and is only waiting for sunset to finish becoming pure.

phrases.english: But weren't they people who had immersed that day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the Sinai separation timeline discussed in the previous part of the sugya
steps.kashyaTarget: The calculated timing of separation and immersion before מתן תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the count leaves some women as טבולי יום at Sinai, then the תורה was given to people who were not fully pure

steps.title: The תורה may be given to a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר רבין and רב חנינא בר אבין answer that the תורה was given to a טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר רבין and רב חנינא בר אבין both said: The תורה was given to a person who immersed that day.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the challenge. They say there is no problem, because the תורה was given to a טבול יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that the people receiving the תורה had to be fully pure. These אמוראים reject that assumption. A טבול יום is pure enough to receive the תורה, so the timeline stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To one who immersed that day

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר רָבִין וְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Ravin and Rav Chanina bar Avin
who both said:
The Torah was given to one who immersed that day.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the facts but denies the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Receiving the תורה requires complete purity, so a טבול יום would be a problem
steps.terutzMaskana: A טבול יום is acceptable for receiving the תורה

steps.title: רבינא asks מרימר what exactly the teaching means
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught this teaching, and רבינא asked him whether the תורה was actually given to a טבול יום or was only fit to be given to one.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר sat and taught this teaching. רבינא said to מרימר: Are you saying the תורה 'was given' to a טבול יום, or are you saying it 'was fit' to be given to one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story in which מרימר repeats the teaching from step 2. רבינא asks him to clarify its exact meaning, and this sets up מרימר's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible readings. Either there really were טבולי יום at Sinai, or the rule only says the תורה could have been given to them. רבינא wants to know which one מרימר meant.

phrases.english: Mareimar sat
and was stating this teaching.
Ravina said to Mareimar:
Are you saying 'was given,' or are you saying 'was fit'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the answer given in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the teaching describes what actually happened or only what would have been allowed

steps.title: מרימר answers: it was only fit to be given
steps.stepSummary: מרימר answers that he meant the תורה was fit to be given to a טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am saying 'was fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר answers רבינא. He meant only that the תורה would have been allowed to be given to a טבול יום, not that this actually happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to one explanation, the people were in fact completely pure at Sinai, and no woman discharged on the third day. The rule still answers the challenge from step 1, because even if there had been a טבול יום, it would not have been a problem.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am saying 'was fit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teaching means the תורה was fit to be given to a טבול יום, not that it actually was

steps.title: Why not immerse and receive the תורה at בין השמשות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people could not have immersed during בין השמשות and then received the תורה right then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them immerse at twilight, and receive the תורה at twilight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a different schedule. Immersing at twilight and receiving the תורה at that time would have avoided waiting until שבת morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is to avoid any delay and any issue of טבול יום. If immersion happened at twilight Friday evening, the תורה could have been given right away. So why wait until morning?

phrases.english: And let them immerse at twilight,
and receive the Torah at twilight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the timing of מתן תורה
steps.kashyaTarget: Delaying מתן תורה until שבת morning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A twilight schedule would seem to work just as well, so the delay looks unnecessary

steps.title: The תורה is not given in darkness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק quotes the פסוק 'From the beginning I did not speak in secret' to show that the תורה had to be given in daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: 'From the beginning I did not speak in secret' (ישעיהו 48:16).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that the תורה had to be given openly, in daylight, and not at twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twilight leads into night, which is a time of concealment. The פסוק teaches that ה׳'s original speech, meaning מתן תורה, was out in the open. So twilight was not an option.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
'From the beginning I did not speak in secret.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source showing the suggested schedule is not allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Twilight would be an acceptable time
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה must be given in open daylight

steps.title: Why not immerse and receive the תורה on שבת morning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people could not have immersed on שבת morning and received the תורה that same morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them immerse on שבת morning, and receive the תורה on שבת morning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another schedule. Immersing on the morning of שבת would allow the תורה to be given in daylight right afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This suggestion solves the 'not in darkness' problem from step 6. Some explain that it would also let the separation period start one עונה later. So why was it not done this way?

phrases.english: And let them immerse on Shabbat morning,
and receive the Torah on Shabbat morning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an alternative schedule that avoids the problem raised in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The actual timing of immersion before מתן תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A daytime schedule on שבת morning seems to meet every requirement

steps.title: Everyone must come to receive the תורה together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that the plan was meant to avoid some people going to receive the תורה while others were going to immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: So that these would not be going to receive the תורה while those were going to immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains why the morning schedule would not work. It would split the nation, since some people would still be at the מקוה when others went to receive the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal was for the entire nation to go to receive the תורה together. A morning immersion would have left some people busy with טבילה at that moment, which would break that unity.
steps.whatToRemember: The timing of מתן תורה was designed so that it happened in daylight and with the whole nation arriving together, not split between the מקוה and Sinai.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַלָּלוּ הוֹלְכִין לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: So that these would not be going to receive the Torah
while those are going to immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַלָּלוּ הוֹלְכִין לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason against the proposed schedule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Immersing on שבת morning would work
steps.terutzMaskana: It would divide the nation at the moment of receiving the תורה

steps.title: חכמים require six complete עונות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the earlier opinions belong to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, but חכמים require six full עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא son of רבי אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: These are the words of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. But חכמים say: We require six complete עונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the law of the משנה. רבי יוחנן reports that חכמים hold a stricter view than רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is a 12-hour period. According to חכמים, semen discharged within six full עונות, which is 72 hours, of relations still makes the woman טמא. Only after that is she טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Periods of twelve hours (day or night)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva,
but the Sages say:
We require six complete periods.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the Sinai discussion to the law in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים require six complete עונות before discharged semen no longer makes her טמא
steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a third, stricter opinion to the debate in the משנה about how long semen stays טמא.

steps.title: The time limit applies only to semen inside a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the dispute applies only to semen discharged from a woman. Semen that left a man stays טמא as long as it is moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The dispute is about semen that came out of a woman. But semen that came out of a man is טמא as long as it is moist.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא limits the dispute to one case. All the time limits apply only to semen discharged from a woman's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside a woman's body, the warmth causes the semen to decay over time, so after a certain number of עונות it is no longer טמא. Semen from a man, for example on a garment, has no such time limit. It stays טמא as long as it is still moist.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is where it came out of a woman,
but where it came out of a man,
it is impure as long as it is moist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute just presented
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Semen from a man stays טמא as long as it is moist, with no time limit

steps.title: רב ששת: the Torah excludes foul semen
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא that excludes foul semen from טומאה and suggests that it refers to semen from a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: 'And every garment and every hide that has semen on it' (ויקרא 15:17) excludes semen that has become foul. Isn't that talking about semen that came out of a man?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב חסדא using a teaching based on the פסוק about garments. That teaching says foul semen is not טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about garments, which suggests semen from a man. If foul semen on a garment is not טמא, then even moist semen from a man can lose its טומאה once it decays. That contradicts רב חסדא's claim that it stays טמא as long as it is moist.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected:
'And every garment and every hide'
'on which there is semen' —
this excludes semen that is foul.
Is it not referring to semen that came out of a man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's rule from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that semen from a man stays טמא as long as it is moist
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says foul semen is excluded, and if it refers to semen from a man, then semen from a man can lose its טומאה even while moist

steps.title: No, the exclusion refers to semen from a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about semen that came out of a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to semen that came out of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It reads the ברייתא as talking about semen discharged from a woman after it decayed inside her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'foul' semen in the ברייתא is semen that sat inside a woman's body past the time limit. So the ברייתא matches רב חסדא's view. The time limit applies only to the woman's case, and his rule about semen from a man stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, semen from a man stays טמא as long as it is moist. The 'foul semen' exclusion applies only to semen that decayed inside a woman.

phrases.english: No, where it came out of a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא refers to semen from a man
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to semen from a woman, so it fits רב חסדא

steps.title: רב פפא's question: a Jew's semen inside a non-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether a Jew's semen inside a גויה decays within the same time frame, and he gives reasons for both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What is the law of a Jew's semen inside a non-Jewish woman? Do we say Jews, who worry about מצוות, have warm bodies, but non-Jews, who do not worry about מצוות, do not? Or perhaps, since they eat שקצים ורמשים, their bodies are also warm?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a question about semen inside the body of a non-Jewish woman. He presents two possible sides without deciding between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timeline assumes that body heat makes the semen decay. One side says a Jew's worry about keeping מצוות heats the body, which would not apply to a גויה. The other side says eating non-kosher creatures also heats the body, so the result would be the same.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּמְעֵי גוֹיָה מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Semen of a Jew inside a non-Jewish woman — what is the law?
Jews, who worry about מצוות — their body is warm,
non-Jews, who do not worry about מצוות — not.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאָכְלִין שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since they eat non-kosher creatures and creeping things,
their body is warm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about semen inside a woman's body
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether semen inside a גויה follows the same time limits for טומאה

steps.title: A follow-up question: semen inside an animal
steps.stepSummary: Assuming a גויה's body is warm, רב פפא asks about semen inside a בהמה, since a בהמה lacks the long passage that a woman has.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that since they eat שקצים ורמשים their bodies are warm, what about inside an animal? Is it a woman, who has a פרוזדור, in whom it becomes foul, but an animal, which has no פרוזדור, in which it does not? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא builds a second question on top of the first one. Even if a גויה is treated like a Jewish woman, would semen inside an animal also decay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new factor is the shape of the body, not body heat. A woman has a long passage called a פרוזדור that may cause the semen to decay. An animal does not have one, so perhaps the semen would not decay, or perhaps it makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (builds a follow-up question)

phrases.english: And if you will say

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָכְלִי שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים חֲבִיל גּוּפַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: that since they eat non-kosher creatures and creeping things their body is warm:
Inside an animal — what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה הִיא דְּאִית לַהּ פְּרוֹזְדוֹר — מַסְרְחָא,
phrases.english: Is it a woman, who has a corridor, in whom it becomes foul,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהֵמָה דְּלֵית לַהּ פְּרוֹזְדוֹר — לָא,
phrases.english: but an animal, which has no corridor, in which it does not?
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a second question, assuming one answer to step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether semen inside a בהמה decays and loses its טומאה like semen inside a woman

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: Both of רב פפא's questions remain unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without answering רב פפא's questions. The questions are left as תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source was found to decide either question. So the law about semen inside a גויה and inside a בהמה remains an open doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand — the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's questions, first about a גויה (body heat) and then about a בהמה (the פרוזדור), both end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions from steps 13-14 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The law about semen inside a גויה or a בהמה remains an unresolved doubt

steps.title: A dispute over the date the עשרת הדברות were given
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. The רבנן say the עשרת הדברות were given on the sixth of the month (סיון). רבי יוסי says the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: On the sixth of the month, the עשרת הדברות were given to ישראל. רבי יוסי says: On the seventh of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that records a disagreement about which day of סיון the תורה was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, connected to the earlier discussion of counting days before מתן תורה. The רבנן say the sixth and רבי יוסי says the seventh. The rest of the sugya will explain where this one-day difference comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: On the sixth of the month
On the seventh of it (the month)

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is the anchor for the whole following sugya. Everything after it explains how each side counts the days.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On the sixth of the month
the Ten Commandments were given to Israel.
Rabbi Yosei says: On the seventh of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּשִׁשִּׁי בַּחֹדֶשׁ נִיתְּנוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רב פפא's unanswered questions about decaying semen to a new topic: the date of מתן תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן say the תורה was given on 6 סיון. רבי יוסי says 7 סיון.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the Jews reached סיני on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides agree that the Jews arrived at מדבר סיני on ראש חודש. He learns this from a גזירה שוה on the word "הזה" ("this").
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that they came to מדבר סיני on ראש חודש. It is written here: "On this day they came to the Sinai desert," and it is written there: "This month shall be for you the head of months." Just as there it means ראש חודש, so too here it means ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins narrowing the מחלוקת by pointing out what both sides agree on. The first shared point is that the arrival at סיני was on ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "ביום הזה באו מדבר סיני" does not say which day it was. The same word "הזה" appears in "החדש הזה," which refers to ראש חודש, so the arrival day is also ראש חודש. This gives both sides a shared starting point for their count.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the month
It is written here... and it is written there (the setup of a גזירה שוה)
Just as there... so too here

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking a side in the מחלוקת here. He is listing points both opinions accept, to isolate the real disagreement.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees that on Rosh Chodesh
they came to the Sinai desert.
It is written here: "On this day
they came to the Sinai desert,"
and it is written there: "This month
shall be for you the head of months" —
just as there it means Rosh Chodesh,
so too here it means Rosh Chodesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲתוֹ לְמִדְבָּר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the ברייתא's מחלוקת by establishing a point both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree the arrival at מדבר סיני was on ראש חודש סיון, learned from a גזירה שוה on "הזה."

steps.title: Everyone agrees the תורה was given on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a second shared point: the תורה was given on שבת. He learns this from a גזירה שוה on the word "זכור."
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone agrees that the תורה was given to ישראל on שבת. It is written here: "Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy," and it is written there: "And משה said to the people: Remember this day." Just as there it was said on that very day, so too here it was said on that very day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second point of agreement: מתן תורה happened on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said "זכור את היום הזה" about יציאת מצרים on the very day they left. So "זכור את יום השבת" in the עשרת הדברות was also said on the very day it speaks of, which is שבת. Now both sides agree on the starting day (ראש חודש) and the weekday of מתן תורה (שבת).

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה was given on שבת
Remember (the shared word linking the two פסוקים)

phrases.english: And everyone agrees that on Shabbat
the Torah was given to Israel.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְקַדְּשׁוֹ״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy,"
and it is written there: "And Moshe said to the people:
Remember this day" —
phrases.notes: שמות יג:ג, said on the day of יציאת מצרים

phrases.english: just as there it was on that very day,
so too here it was on that very day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second point of agreement to the first one in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree מתן תורה was on שבת, learned from a גזירה שוה on "זכור."

steps.title: The real dispute: which weekday was ראש חודש, and רבי יוסי's timeline begins
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about which weekday ראש חודש fell on. רבי יוסי holds it was Sunday. On Sunday nothing was said because the people were tired from traveling. On Monday they were told "ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים."
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is about the setting of the month. רבי יוסי holds: The month was set on Sunday. On Sunday He did not say anything to them, because of the weariness from the journey. On Monday He said to them: "And you shall be for Me a kingdom of priests."
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the shared points are clear, the גמרא pinpoints the real disagreement. It begins laying out רבי יוסי's day-by-day count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides agree on ראש חודש arrival and a שבת מתן תורה, the date difference must come from which weekday ראש חודש was. רבי יוסי says Sunday, which makes the following שבת the 7th. His timeline opens with a day of rest for the tired travelers, then the message of "ממלכת כהנים" on Monday, and it continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The setting of the month (which weekday ראש חודש fell on)
Sunday (the first day of the week)
Monday (the second day of the week)

steps.confusionAlert: "חד בשבא" does not mean "on Shabbat." It means "the first day of the week" (Sunday). Here "שבא" means "week."
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a disagreement about dates into a disagreement about the calendar. Both sides read the פסוקים the same way. They only differ on which weekday the month began.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is about the setting of the month:
Rabbi Yosei holds —
the month was set on Sunday,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחַד בְּשַׁבָּא לָא אֲמַר לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
phrases.english: and on Sunday He did not say anything at all to them
because of the weariness from the journey;
on Monday He said to them:
"And you shall be for Me a kingdom of priests";
phrases.notes: שמות יט:ו. The timeline continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out the shared assumptions in steps 17–18, it identifies the actual point of dispute and begins רבי יוסי's timeline.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת depends on which weekday ראש חודש fell on. רבי יוסי says Sunday: nothing was said that day, and "ממלכת כהנים" was said on Monday.
